newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OZ boosts H1 profit, to buy back shares.
newsitem.headline: OZ boosts H1 profit, to buy back shares.

text.p: OZ Holding, a holding company that invests in financial services companies, said group profit in the first six months of 1997 rose to 40.7 million Swiss francs from 18.8 million last year and it was making an offer to buy back its own shares.
OZ, part of Martin Ebner's BZ Group, also said in a statement that it was offering to buy back 60,000 shares at a maximum price of 740 francs.
The offer is open until July 8 and the board of directors will propose to an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on August 8 that share capital be cut by a maximum 600,000 francs.
In the last quarter, BZ Group Holding reduced its stake in OZ Holding to 25 percent, or 150,000 shares, from 53.3 percent, or 320,000 shares.
On June 30, OZ Holding's equity, after a dividend payment of 18 million francs, rose to 197 million, or 328 francs per share from 175 million, or 291 francs per share end-December, 1996.
On a per-share basis, the six-month profit amounts to 67.80 francs, up from 31 francs in the same 1996 period. Income from securities was 36 million and commission income 14.9 million.
OZ Holding's participations include OZ Zurich AG and OM Gruppen AB of Stockholm.
